$comment: CANONICAL FILE. axRange vendors a byte-identical copy and compares it by test, so edit it in aximprint and copy, never the other way round. Formatting is mechanical: `json.dumps(doc, sort_keys=True, indent=2)` plus a trailing newline.  ---  NINE REFUSALS THIS SCHEMA CANNOT EXPRESS, named so a consumer does not read schema-valid as parser-accepted: (1) a segment/conduit CIDR must be the NETWORK address (`ipaddress.ip_network(strict=True)`), so `10.80.31.5/24` matches `$defs.cidr` and the parser refuses it; the IPv6 alternative in that pattern is deliberately loose for the same reason. (2) A conduit joins two DIFFERENT segments, so `10.0.0.0/24|10.0.0.0/24` matches `$defs.conduitKey` and the parser refuses it; the parser also CANONICALIZES a conduit key by sorting its two halves, so either authored order is accepted and the sorted one is what a re-emit writes. (3) `as_of` must parse as ISO-8601 (`datetime.fromisoformat`, with a bare `Z` accepted); `format` is annotation-only in draft 2020-12, so an unparseable string validates here. (4) Two records in one block sharing a merge key are refused ((kind,key) for add, (key,field) for override, key for suppress). (5) One key in both `add` and `suppress` is refused. (6) One (key,field) declared by both an `add` record's own field and an `override` is refused. (7) A link joins two DIFFERENT devices, so `mac:a#p1|mac:a#p2` matches `$defs.linkKey` and the parser refuses it; the parser also canonicalizes a link key by sorting its two ends. (8) A `device` add names its `device_kind` and a `link` add its `mode` with a shape that fits it (an access link carries exactly one `vlans` entry and no `native`; a trunk names `vlans` and/or `native`), which is a relation between a record's fields. (9) One key in both `confirm` and `doubt` is refused. Four, five, six and nine are cross-record and no per-instance keyword reaches them.  ---  axr-assertions/2 (2026-11-07, docs/design/topology-layers.md section 3.2) is a superset of /1: a /1 document parses unchanged and is re-emitted as /2.  ---  A YAML document is validated as its JSON projection: a YAML timestamp scalar is its ISO-8601 string, and `imprint: null` is JSON null.

addRecord.description: Discriminated by `kind`. `kind: route` is refused BY NAME: a twin config has no route object at all -- inter-segment reachability belongs to the synthetic gateway, and `kind: conduit` is how it is authored. `device`, `link` and `tap` are the device tree's records (axr-assertions/2, docs/design/topology-layers.md section 3.2); a `device` add always names its `device_kind`, and a `link` add its `mode` (an access link carries exactly one `vlans` entry and no `native`; a trunk names `vlans` and/or `native`) -- both are parser refusals a per-record keyword does not reach, see refusal 8.

oneOf.title: add a conduit the vantage did not supply
add a host the vantage did not supply
add a segment the vantage did not supply
add a device (a switch, or a router) the vantage did not supply
add a link between two device ports
add a tap on a segment or a device port

cidr.description: A segment key, and the value of a `segment` field: the OBSERVED CIDR, which must be the network address (see the top-level $comment, refusal 1). A bare address with no prefix is accepted and means /32 or /128.

cidrList.description: The segments a trunk carries tagged (an access link: exactly one), as observed CIDRs; deduplicated and sorted on re-emit.

conduitKey.description: Exactly two CIDRs joined by a single '|'. The two must differ and are canonicalized into sorted order (see the top-level $comment, refusal 2).

deviceKind.description: What a device IS. A `kind: device` add takes router or switch; an override of a discovered host's `device_kind` may also say host, to turn a device back into one.

evidenceClass.description: DOCUMENTATION ONLY -- no key in this document carries an evidence class. Published here because the class is a property of the CHANNEL: every fact from this file is `asserted`, the first entry, and the tuple's ORDER is the precedence order (highest first). FIVE IS THE INTENDED SHAPE HERE, not a divergence from axRange's six-class model: that model's sixth class, `compiler`, is by definition a SIDECAR-ONLY label for a value the compiler invented -- it never appears in the IR and is never assertable, so it cannot be one of the classes this document ranks. The two are consistent; a consumer joining on this enum wants exactly these five.

groupName.description: A member split: the node group this host joins instead of the one its role, segment and presence would put it in. A non-empty identifier with no whitespace, like a segment name.

hostKey.description: A host entity key in the self-describing `<key_kind>:<value>` form the IR mints -- address:, hostname:, mac: -- never a twin-config index. The value after the colon must not be blank. Since /2 the value may not contain '#' or '|', the port and link separators.

linkKey.description: Two device ports joined by a single '|': each end is `<host key>#<port>` (`mac:aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff#P14`). The two devices must differ and the ends are canonicalized into sorted order (see the top-level $comment, refusal 7).

markKey.description: What a confirm or doubt record may mark: a host key, a segment CIDR or a link key.

note.description: REQUIRED on every record. An assertion outranks every class of evidence in the store, so the reason it was made is the only thing that makes it reviewable later. A whitespace-only note is refused.

overrideRecord.description: The kind is DERIVED from the key's shape, never authored: an `address:`/`hostname:`/`mac:` key is a host (a device is a host entity), a CIDR is a segment, and two device ports joined by '|' are a link. A conduit and a tap have no overridable field.

field.description: CLOSED, per kind: what is overridable on a host.
CLOSED, per kind: what is overridable on a segment.
CLOSED, per kind: what is overridable on a link.

oneOf.title: override an asserted or discovered link

portList.description: A listen or dial census for a host nothing observed. Parsed into the `"<port>/<proto>"` strings `ir_entity.listen_ports` already carries, deduplicated and sorted; a re-emit writes the `{port, proto}` form back. The protocol set is closed because its producer is the sensor's own `proto` column, so a value outside it would match nothing.

additionalProperties.description: A boolean is not an integer here.

resources.description: CLOSED to cpu/disk/ram, mirroring the role catalog's own rows. axRange's `twin_config` is `extra="forbid"`, so a fourth key is refused at deploy time, one repo and several hours later. An empty block asserts nothing and is refused.

segmentName.description: A non-empty identifier with no whitespace -- it is what a node's `net:` references.

sensorList.description: The sensors a tap delivers to, by the names the tap plan and adapter.conf use; deduplicated and sorted on re-emit.

tapKey.description: Where a tap sits: a whole segment (`segment:<cidr>`) or one device port (`port:<host key>#<port>`).

zoneType.description: axRange's two SDN zone shapes. A cast emits `simple` for every segment as a `compiler` choice ('no VLAN evidence exists at this vantage'); asserting `vlan` is the worked example.

description: The operator assertions file: what an operator ADDS that the vantage could not see (hosts, segments, conduits, and since /2 devices, links and taps), OVERRIDES that it inferred wrongly, SUPPRESSES as out of scope, and CONFIRMS or DOUBTS (pins as asserted, or marks unconfirmed). Written by axRange's Console and read by `aximprint cast --assertions`. Every fact it carries is evidence class `asserted`, the top of the precedence order in `$defs.evidenceClass`; confidence is never authored and is 1.0 by convention. PRODUCER OF RECORD: `src/aximprint/operator_assertions.py` in the aximprint repo -- this document states what that parser accepts, and where the two disagree the parser is right and this file is a bug.

add.description: Entities the vantage did not supply. An empty list is fine; null is not -- the key is either absent or a list.

as_of.description: REQUIRED: this snapshot's time bound, and the `window_start` of every row the reference ingest writes. An import with no time bound cannot be compared with anything else.

confirm.description: Discovered entities the operator pins as `asserted`, fields unchanged. Keyed like an override.

doubt.description: Discovered entities the operator marks `unconfirmed` (a cast's weak-evidence verdict, pinned). A key in both `confirm` and `doubt` is refused (refusal 9).

imprint.description: OPTIONAL: which imprint these assertions are about. A present but empty string is refused; an explicit null is accepted and means the same as absent.

override.description: Fields of DISCOVERED entities, replaced by a hand-authored value.

schema.description: Fail closed on an unknown schema rather than guessing which records it meant.

source.description: REQUIRED: `operator:<name>`, case-insensitive, with a non-empty name. An assertion's source is a PERSON, and saying so in the value is what lets a scorecard's evidence mix tell 'an operator said so' from 'an export said so'. Canonicalized to `operator:<name>` on re-emit.

suppress.description: Entities that are out of scope for this twin. HOST KEYS ONLY: a segment key is refused, because removing a segment that still carries placed hosts is a topology edit rather than a suppression.
